falsifiable_hypothesis: Targetwise EB reliabilities are noisy with only three inner folds. Treating the 24 cross-fitted target contrasts as one multivariate mean-estimation problem permits a lower-variance positive-part James-Stein shrinkage toward zero.
component_rule: Orientation A is the leave-one-whole-patient bagged geometry prediction. Orientation B starts from interpolated-jackknife geometry. No A/B prediction averaging is performed.
calibration_rule: Within each outer-training partition use the authenticated three inner whole-patient bandwidth-0.7 OOF predictions at the already-selected spectral option. Compute the three targetwise contrast vectors c[k,:], their mean cbar and per-target variance-of-mean v. Let sigma2=mean(v), p=24, and a_JS=max(0,1-(p-2)*sigma2/sum_t cbar[t]^2). Define s=1/8+(7/8)*a_JS and apply q_B=q_B,interpolated_jackknife-0.5*s*cbar. The positive-part James-Stein factor is one scalar shared across all 24 targets in that outer partition. There is no strength grid, target/fold outer-outcome routing, or protected data.

task_contract.ab_rule: average separately costed A/B losses; never average predictions
